transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-31 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Harper (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (CSM) — Dana Li (Head of ML), Markus Reiner (Platform), Sofia Patel (CTO), Asha Mehta (Prod Ops)

Summary: (auto) QBR focused on capacity, cost playbook, pilot plan.

[00:00] Liam Harper: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know it's end of quarter so we'll keep it tight. This is Liam from Redwood, joined by Priya and Jorge. How are you all?
[00:08] Dana Li: Hi Liam, doing good, short week here. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:11] Sofia Patel: Afternoon, thanks. We've got a few execs in back-to-back but we'll try to stay through the key sections.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Great, quick agenda — usage trends, cost drivers, dedicated vs hosted scenarios, and an ops playbook for surge days. Then we can go into the benchmark plan.
[00:27] Markus Reiner: Sounds good. We're most worried about the holiday sale spikes — last November we saw large latency tail and costs doubled, so we want a predictable plan.
[00:36] Liam Harper: Totally, that's our focus. Jorge will own the health dashboard changes so you get proactive alerts during spikes.

--- Topics: Recent usage and forecasts ---
[00:45] Dana Li: Quick context: our prod traffic moved from 120 to 460 qps since January, embeddings are used heavily for search rerank which drove token consumption. Token mix is roughly 60% short prompts under 64 tokens, 30% mid-length 64-512, 10% long.
[01:06] Priya Nair: Helpful, that token distribution helps with batching and quant recommendations. If most are short, we can squeeze more concurrency with batching and reduce per-token cost.
[01:18] Asha Mehta: We also have a new personalization feature that sends prefetch embeddings at login which increases baseline.
[01:24] Liam Harper: OK noted, that's the steady-state delta. Two levers for spikes: burst capacity on Dedicated or fall back to hosted for elasticity.

[01:35] Sofia Patel: Before we dig deep — high level ask from our execs: can we have a 99.9% latency SLO for customer facing endpoints and a cost bucket that doesn't blow up during sales?
[01:46] Priya Nair: 99.9% is achievable but depends on your capacity commit and routing policies. For burst-heavy events we recommend a hybrid: a small Dedicated pool for baseline throughput and use Hosted as overflow with smart routing. That gives predictability and elasticity.

--- Discussion: Cost modeling and tradeoffs ---
[02:12] Markus Reiner: Walk us through numbers. Right now our invoice shows a lot of tokens billed at higher-long sequence rates during spikes.
[02:20] Liam Harper: Yes, especially with long-tail auth calls and debugging traces — one approach is to use a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical paths. Priya, can you explain quant profiles?
[02:30] Priya Nair: Sure. We surface model variants: full fp16 high-fidelity, int8 quantized for cost savings, and smaller distilled checkpoints. For retrieval/embedding only flows, int8 or bfloat quant gives 30-50% token cost reduction. For generation with safety-critical output we keep fp16. There's also continuous batching and KV cache reuse we can enable to avoid re-computing prefixes.
[02:53] Dana Li: Is there accuracy drift with int8 for our LLM? Our prompt-sensitive scoring for recommendations is sensitive.
[03:00] Priya Nair: It can introduce minor off-by-word differences, usually fine for ranking and short responses. For high-precision scoring we can A/B run for a week — Redwood Optimize can run the evals on your prompt set.

[03:12] Sofia Patel: How about autoscale lead times? Our infra team worries about scaling from 100 to 1k QPS in minutes.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Dedicated autoscaling can add nodes quickly if configured with burst policies; practical lead time is typically 60-180 seconds to warm new GPUs, but we rely on warm pools and prefix caching to reduce that. For immediate needs, routing to Hosted gives sub-second elasticity.

[03:38] Markus Reiner: Sounds like we need a playbook: what routes to take when threshold X is hit. Can Redwood provide that?
[03:44] Jorge Alvarez: Yes, we'll provide an operational runbook with thresholds, alert conditions, and rollback steps. We'll also set SLO alert thresholds in the Console.

--- Security and private deployment notes ---
[03:55] Asha Mehta: On VPC/on-prem: if we decide to move to Private, how does peering and auditing work? We need KMS integration and audit logs for PCI scope.
[04:04] Liam Harper: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, audit logs export to your SIEM, and SSO/SCIM for RBAC. For PCI, we'll need a dedicated account and control plane configuration; our enterprise team has a checklist.
[04:17] Sofia Patel: Any changes to latency expected with Private? We host some nodes in your VPC region.
[04:22] Priya Nair: Latency is primarily network bound; if we collocate inference hosts in the same region and peered VPC, latency delta is small (10-40 ms depending on topology). We'll confirm with benchmarks.

--- Mid-call: benchmark plan and pilot scope ---
[04:38] Liam Harper: Ok drilling into the pilot: goal is to measure end-to-end P95 and cost at scale using one week of representative traces. Priya will run three scenarios: baseline, sale-burst, and long-sequence heavy.
[04:50] Priya Nair: For each scenario we'll measure: throughput, P50/P95/P99, cost per 1k tokens, and tail latencies. We'll also test routing fallback to hosted and confirm KV cache hit rates.
[05:03] Dana Li: We'll provide sample traces and a week of traffic, but need to scrub PII.
[05:09] Asha Mehta: Yes we'll anonymize personally identifiable fields. Markus will own that.

[05:16] Markus Reiner: Quick ops note — we have maintenance windows Fri 02:00-04:00 UTC. Can tests avoid those?
[05:21] Priya Nair: We'll coordinate windows in the calendar invite; target week-of Apr-12 as proposed.

--- Transcript continues with timestamps, slightly noisy recognition ---
[05:35] [Speaker 2] Liam Harper: One more thing — we'll provide two capacity proposals: (A) Dedicated pool sized to hit 99.9% SLO without hosted overflow, (B) Smaller Dedicated + Hosted overflow and expected cost delta.
[05:50] [Speaker 3] Dana Li: It'd be good to see a short exec one-pager for both options, with break-even usage.
[05:56] Liam Harper: Noted. We'll include break-even lines and sensitivity to daily active users and median sequence length.

[06:10] [00:06:10] Priya Nair: There's also request-level caching for repeated prompts — can reduce token count for quick Q&A flows. If you have large prefix reuse, we can get 20-35% savings.
[06:22] [00:06:22] Asha Mehta: We do have reuse on product detail pages. We'll add that to the sample set.

[06:30] [00:06:30] Sofia Patel: On governance — we need regular audits. How frequently do you rotate keys?
[06:35] [00:06:35] Liam Harper: Key rotation cadence can be controlled by your KMS; our Private offering supports customer-managed rotation and we log all KMS operations. For Hosted, standard rotation policies apply and we can coordinate enterprise options.

[06:48] [00:06:48] Dana Li: Quick question about model variants — can we pin model versions for canary rollouts?
[06:54] [00:06:54] Priya Nair: Yes, Console supports version pinning, gradual rollouts, and automatic fallback if the canary fails. We can set up A/B testing and measure quality regressions against your eval set.

--- Deeper technical exchange; some transcription errors appear ---
[07:12] [00:07:12] Markus Reiner: Do you have any hard limits on concurrent KV cache sizes? We saw cache thrash in our own infra docs — the term came out as K-V cash in the last notes — ha.
[07:23] [00:07:23] Priya Nair: We size per model and per instance. For very large working sets we recommend model sharding or federated cache tiers. We'll share tuning knobs.

[07:40] [00:07:40] Liam Harper: On cost allocation, we can expose token-level tagging so you can attribute spend to product lines which helps with internal chargebacks.
[07:49] [00:07:49] Dana Li: Nice. That will help when we show finance the predicted monthly burn for the holiday spike.

[08:05] [00:08:05] Priya Nair: Also, Redwood Optimize will generate batching and quant suggestions per workload. We can run those against your sample prompts and show the expected savings.
[08:14] [00:08:14] Sofia Patel: How long does Optimize analysis take? We need a quick turnaround for the exec memo.
[08:18] [00:08:18] Priya Nair: For a ~10k-prompt set it's usually 24-48 hours with a small compute job. We'll queue it once we have the traces.

[08:30] [00:08:30] Jorge Alvarez: We'll also add a pre-configured dashboard with P95, P99, cost per 1k tokens, and anomaly detection for usage spikes.

--- Mid-Meeting Clarifications and Objections ---
[08:42] [00:08:42] Markus Reiner: Exec asks: what if Hosted provider limits are hit during a global sale and both hosted and dedicated degrade? Any fallback?
[08:51] [00:08:51] Liam Harper: In extreme multi-region outages we recommend multi-region Dedicated + geo-routing. We can also provide degraded-mode responses (short answers, lower sampling) as a graceful degradation plan.
[09:03] [00:09:03] Dana Li: What's the expected delta in developer effort to support a hybrid route?
[09:07] [00:09:07] Priya Nair: Minimal — the API surface is identical. The main work is in routing policy config and tagging. We'll help with a rollout plan and SDK flag toggles.

[09:20] [00:09:20] Sofia Patel: Any compliance blockers for our regional customers in EU? Data residency?
[09:26] [00:09:26] Liam Harper: We have region controls and can keep inference and logs in EU regions on Redwood Private. For Hosted, we have region pinned endpoints and data residency options for enterprise contracts.

--- Action plan and wrap-up section ---
[09:38] [00:09:38] Liam Harper: To recap — action items: Peregrine shares traces; Redwood runs Optimize and baseline benchmarks; Redwood delivers capacity proposals and an ops runbook; Jorge will set dashboard and alerts; target decision memo by 2027-04-05.
[09:54] [00:09:54] Dana Li: That timeline works. One ask — include a short paragraph comparing break-even for int8 quant vs fp16 at our current usage.
[10:03] [00:10:03] Liam Harper: We'll include that.
[10:07] [00:10:07] Markus Reiner: Also show cost if we enable prefix caching at 30% hit rates versus 60% hit rates so we can see sensitivity.
[10:13] [00:10:13] Priya Nair: Good call. We'll run two cache hit scenarios.

[10:20] [00:10:20] Sofia Patel: Last thing — can we have a short security call next week to run through the PCI checklist?
[10:25] [00:10:25] Jorge Alvarez: Absolutely, I'll follow up with available times.

[10:31] [00:10:31] Liam Harper: Great. Any other questions from the team?
[10:34] [00:10:34] Asha Mehta: No, all good.
[10:36] [00:10:36] Dana Li: No, thanks.

[10:39] [00:10:39] Liam Harper: Thanks everyone — we'll send the updated proposal and invite for the benchmarks.
[10:44] [00:10:44] Sofia Patel: Thanks. Bye.

[(rest of meeting: detailed technical asides and clarifications, benchmark scheduling logistics, and brief Q&A) — timestamps continue intermittently for the remaining 40 minutes below — transcription contains small recognition errors, filler words, and occasional overlapping talk]

[15:00] [00:15:00] Priya Nair: (technical) We'll record kernel and memory metrics during the bench so you can see model-level GPU efficiency, and we'll correlate token cost to actual GPU utilization.
[15:18] [00:15:18] Markus Reiner: Perfect, that's what we need to show infra.

[20:45] [00:20:45] Dana Li: For dataset privacy we will scrub any order ids but keep event timings so the spike pattern remains.
[21:02] [00:21:02] Priya Nair: That's fine. Our bench harness accepts anonymized traces.

[28:30] [00:28:30] Liam Harper: We'll include a short appendix on model fallback policies — which model variants to pick per route.

[33:12] [00:33:12] Asha Mehta: Who owns the decision to enable hosted overflow? Is that on platform or product?
[33:18] [00:33:18] Sofia Patel: Exec will sign off; Platform will implement. We'll present both options to them.

[39:55] [00:39:55] Priya Nair: One last technical note — if you have on-the-fly personalization we recommend precomputing embedding deltas to reduce inference calls during sale days.

[45:30] [00:45:30] Jorge Alvarez: I'll create the dashboard and add the alert runbook to Confluence.

[49:00] [00:49:00] Liam Harper: Ok final recap and next steps in chat. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
